title: Cipher passage in a German report to Hesse-Kassel, Thirty Years' War (HStAM 4 d Nr. 1218 no. 49; DECODE R4500)

plaintext.source: Contemporary interlinear decipherment over cipher lines 1-4 only.

transcription.notes: --measure counts 654 including 64 word-space marks; 590 signs. Lines 1-2 cramped under a faded gloss.

system.summary: Letter substitution written mostly in digits (0-9) plus a few signs (theta, triangle, d-shaped sign, w-sign, crossed t, crossed 4); '12' written together is r; a few homophones (a: 5, A; s: 2, F).
system.sibling_key: none found; four sign alphabets of the same volume (R4467, R4491, R4520, R4525) do not fit

prior_solution.where: interlinear contemporary decipherment on lines 1-4 of the letter itself

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched R4500 with the session cookie; one page, German clear letter with 14 cipher lines, interlinear gloss on lines 1-4.
First token transcription from line crops; misread the gloss/cipher alignment.
Many-to-one annealing on de-1500s without word spaces: letter-frequency noise only.
EM alignment of gloss 'das kann dieses orths selber observiren' to cipher line 3; inconsistent mappings.
Downloaded all 126 records of the volume (R4452-R4577); compared sign alphabets R4467, R4491, R4520, R4525.
Re-transcribed all 14 lines from mid-resolution views keeping word spaces.
Annealing with word spaces, '12' as one unit, seeded und/under; produced 'entschuldigt', 'damit ich', 'underthenigst'.
Fixed 5=a, q=m, D=l, 2=s, X=b by context; then M=w, 8=o from the gloss.
Gloss phrases 'zumahl nicht', 'etwas tentiret werden', 'dieses orths halber', 'dagegen' come out of lines 3-5 with the rebuilt key.
Read lines 3-14; lines 1-2 do not decode as transcribed.
Second pass on lines 1-2: restored dropped initial signs; line 2 reads, line 1 opens 'die landts...'.

Correction reported while quotations were pulled for Lasry's list, checked on the scan at 3x: the first three signs of line 9 (F 6 12), marked unread as blotted, are clear and give 'ser' with the key unchanged, so 'die|ser ue st ung' = 'dieser Vestung' (9 = u/v) replaces the conjecture 'dieser [sachen]'; in line 11 the signs hidden by '...' after 'nochmals' give 's a l er' with a doubling bar on the triangle, so 'nochmals allerunderthenigst und underthenigst'. 14 of 538 signs unread (was 17).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 524 tokens, 21 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.212 per letter; random keys -5.481 (z 5.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.479 (mean -3.55, z 31.6); annealer on the real text -2.179. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): cipher_tokens.txt and the sign-by-sign reading_tokens.txt; the normalised reading and the key table copied from NOTES.md to texts/R4500_decryption.md and texts/key.md.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): reading_tokens.txt and the normalised reading read through. Lines 8-14 build one clean German sentence (kept read, reviewed B); lines 1-7 are garbled or conjecture in brackets and were split into a second entry, decoded, not read. Class read -> read in part; fraction_read 0.974 (signs with a value) -> 0.52.

Lines 1-7: DECODE R4500 record and image re-opened (no attachment, no DOC text); the contemporary gloss of ll. 1-4 re-read at 2x on native crops and aligned with reading_tokens.txt: matches at 'dieses orts halber', 'dagegen denselben', 'etwas tentiert werden solte', 'zumahl nicht unbewandt'; not at 'insonderheit' (l. 2) or 'observiren' (l. 3). No label or key value changed.

Partial reading of cipher lines 1-7 written (texts/R4500_l01-07_reading.md, log R4500_l01-07_reread_log.md), aligned word by word with the decode; ll. 4-7 build a clause ('gebührender manutenirung der Keiserm. Mait. und des Reichs'), ll. 1-3 do not. b17_score.py (de): 0.00 (0/5), explicit holes 0.20 (1/5). Kept decoded, not read; blocker illegible.

outcome.method_basis: The substitution was rebuilt by homophonic annealing against a 1500s German model, seeded with repeated 'und'/'under' patterns; the contemporary interlinear gloss on cipher lines 1-4 of R4500 served as the control and fixed two values (M = w, 8 = o).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: signs in the cipher lines that read as sentences, ll. 8-14 = 280 of 538 (reading_tokens.txt); ll. 1-7 (258) are decoded, not read. Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.974 = reading_tokens.txt: 538 cipher signs (12 joined = one), 14 marked ? unread.

texts.label: R4500, HStAM 4 d Nr. 1218 no. 49: cipher lines 8-14
texts.summary: A German Thirty Years' War letter in the Hesse-Kassel files reporting troop movements in clear, with the last 14 lines in cipher. The writer, an officer or agent on the imperial side writing from a fortress, reports that he has set out the needs of this fortress to the Emperor and to the Elector of Bavaria, so that he may be held excused and not be found wanting in his report.

reading_review.note: This entry: cipher lines 8-14 (280 of 538 signs, from 'dahero'). reading_tokens.txt gives one clean German sentence, one sign open (the writer has set out the needs of this fortress to the Emperor and the Elector of Bavaria, so that he may be held excused). Lines 1-7 are split off as decoded, not read.
